title: 2026-10-28_Linux_P2P_Ransom_Botnet_Investigation_03c
description: Investigate a compromised system infected with the Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware, identify indicators of compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware. This malware combines ransomware capabilities with botnet functionality, spreading through peer-to-peer networks and encrypting files on infected systems. It also has command-and-control (C2) capabilities, allowing it to receive instructions from remote servers and participate in botnet activities.

Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the indicators of compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Identify the Command-and-Control Server IP Address
levels.content:
Identify the command-and-control server IP address used by the ransomware.

**Hint:** Check network connections and process communications on the victim host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the command-and-control server?
levels.solution:
To identify the command-and-control server IP address, you can use tools like `netstat` or `ss` to check network connections on the victim host. Look for suspicious connections to external IPs.

For example, you can run the following command:
```bash
netstat -tuln
```

This will list all active network connections. Look for connections to external IPs that are not part of your internal network.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `netstat` or `ss` to check network connections on the victim host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for suspicious connections to external IPs that are not part of your internal network.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `netstat -tuln` and look for connections to IPs outside your network range.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port Used for Suspicious Command-and-Control Communication
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

**Hint:** Investigate network traffic and process communications on the victim host.

**Question:** What is the port number used for command-and-control communication?
levels.solution:
To determine the network port used for suspicious command-and-control communication, you can use tools like `netstat` or `ss` to check network connections on the victim host. Look for suspicious ports that are open and being used by unknown processes.

For example, you can run the following command:
```bash
netstat -tuln
```

This will list all active network connections. Look for suspicious ports that are open and being used by unknown processes.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `netstat` or `ss` to check network connections on the victim host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for suspicious ports that are open and being used by unknown processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the output of `netstat -tuln` for unusual port numbers.

levels.title: Identify the External Host Receiving Sensitive Data
levels.content:
Identify the external host receiving sensitive data from the compromised system.

**Hint:** Analyze outbound network traffic and SSH connections on the victim host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the exfiltration server?
levels.solution:
To identify the external host receiving sensitive data from the compromised system, you can use tools like `ss` or `tcpdump` to analyze outbound network traffic and SSH connections on the victim host. Look for connections to external IPs that are receiving data.

For example, you can run the following command:
```bash
ss -tuln
```

This will list all active network connections. Look for connections to external IPs that are receiving data.
